53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

4:49.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:49.en: Hast thou not seen those who praise themselves for purity? Nay, Allah purifieth whom He will, and they will not be wronged even the hair upon a date-stone

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women, because Allah hath made the one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their property (for the support of women). So good women are the obedient, guarding in secret that which Allah hath guarded. As for those from whom ye fear rebellion, admonish them and banish them to beds apart, and scourge them. Then if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Lo! Allah is ever High, Exalted, Great

BKK5ItH3ve0.speaker: adnan
BKK5ItH3ve0.speaker_note: continues his own MWN self-value series; mentions his competitive chess and his work; single speaker
BKK5ItH3ve0.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Value, Episode 40
BKK5ItH3ve0.one_line: Vanity as claiming credit for outcomes, and three things it breeds: entitlement, inflated expectations of Allah, and fear-driven mediocrity.
BKK5ItH3ve0.summary: Starting from the hadith that self-admiration is one of three destroyers, he defines vanity as claiming to know how much credit one deserves for good outcomes. Each person is a recipe of upbringing, gifts and Allah's facilitation, so we should praise Allah, ask Him to credit us, and assume the best of others' achievements while applying this only to ourselves. Vanity grows on entitlement. Before Allah we are owed nothing beyond the justice He bound Himself to; life itself is an unpayable debt, and the only worldly promises are trials and, for those who understand, serenity. He compares an ungrateful child in a room full of gifts, and a debtor demanding a further loan, to how we sound complaining to Allah. Expectations should be modest of people, high of oneself, and absent toward Allah, replaced by hope and dua. A nonbeliever who accepts these realities often copes better than a Muslim who does not. Finally, vanity breeds mediocrity: fearing the verdict on their best, people hold back effort, hide behind humour or ignore feedback. Investing the heart rather than the ego in one's work, welcoming honest critique and pursuing truth over self-validation are the remedies, together with confidence in Allah-given potential and gratitude.

outline.heading: Opening
Self-admiration as one of three destroyers
outline.gist: The hadith names a man's admiration of himself; the problem is not judging one's work good but the bias that makes everything one does great.

outline.heading: Vanity is claiming credit for outcomes
outline.gist: It appears mostly in success: graduating, wealth, awards; no one knows how much of the outcome one's own effort earned.

outline.heading: Do not claim purity; we are all recipes
outline.gist: Only Allah declares who is praiseworthy; our outcomes mix our choices with upbringing, intellect, schools, mentors and His facilitation.

outline.heading: Praise Allah and ask Him to credit you
outline.gist: Give full effort, direct the praise to Allah, and hope He attributes the good to you without claiming it yourself.

outline.heading: Good assumptions about others, low estimates for yourself
outline.gist: Assume others fully earned their success, but about yourself you know how much was the hand you were dealt.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah is not applied to others
outline.gist: Projecting this onto others makes you repellent and arrogant; praise people for their work and be honest only with yourself.

outline.heading: Vanity needs no audience; arrogance does
outline.gist: Vanity is about how you credit yourself even alone, while arrogance requires someone to compare yourself to.

outline.heading: Entitlement: what do you deserve?
outline.gist: With people you deserve fair treatment and should demand it; the question is what you think you are owed by Allah and by life.

outline.heading: Entitled to nothing
outline.gist: We are owed only what Allah bound Himself to, justice, reward, punishment and resurrection, all after death; worldly entitlement is a first-world problem.

outline.heading: Life itself is an unpayable debt
outline.gist: Being alive and able to think already exceeds anything we could repay; everything else is extra generosity.

outline.heading: No one likes entitled people
outline.gist: Entitlement is the biggest turnoff in any relationship, and the best-liked people feel they deserve little, though this does not mean being a doormat.

outline.heading: Treating Allah like Aladdin's lamp
outline.gist: 'I prayed and avoided sin, so why didn't I get it?' misunderstands the relationship and leads to shaken faith, depression and resentment.

outline.heading: The worldly promise: trials
outline.gist: Allah's promises are almost all for after death; in this life believers are promised tests.

outline.heading: The second promise: serenity
outline.gist: A right understanding brings a calmer life, though clinical mental illness is not a sign of weak faith and should not be framed that way.

outline.heading: The entitled child
outline.gist: Parents who had nothing resent children who have everything yet demand more, which builds walls between them.

outline.heading: How our complaints look to Allah
outline.gist: The contrast is far greater: He created us from nothing and gave us everything, yet we sulk over one missing thing.

outline.heading: Zoom out after a failure
outline.gist: He tells disappointed young people their life is the dream of most humans; feel the sadness, but count what you hold.

outline.heading: The debtor demanding another loan
outline.gist: Losing faith and confidence over a setback is like owing a million and shouting that you deserve another thousand.

outline.heading: Allah leaves the gifts and sends the trials
outline.gist: Unlike parents who confiscate, He usually leaves our blessings hoping we notice; stand firm, and keep reinforcing this understanding.

outline.heading: Already maxed out
outline.gist: Seeing everything beyond what we have as a bonus makes us grateful, and gratitude brings more; it is the cure for vanity.

outline.heading: Expectations set satisfaction
outline.gist: In marriage, spouses must agree what is expected in every domain, since unmet expectations make people miserable.

outline.heading: Calibrating expectations of children, staff and spouses
outline.gist: Too high sets people up to fail and feel belittled, too low breeds laziness; he has seen men crushed by expectations they could never meet.

outline.heading: Expect little from people
outline.gist: Low expectations make everything a bonus; the Quran keeps marital duties minimal, and the rest is generosity.

outline.heading: Expect much of yourself, nothing of Allah
outline.gist: Toward Allah have hopes, good assumptions and dua, not expectations; He will show the seeker a path.

outline.heading: Expecting a spouse, a job, a long life
outline.gist: Expecting Allah to arrange our wishes is entitlement rooted in vanity; it comes down to what we think we are.

outline.heading: Watch primates and children to see the nafs
outline.gist: Without guidance, primates and children show the raw nafs chasing superiority; we often let it set our relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: A nonbeliever who gets this copes better
outline.gist: These realities apply regardless of faith; a nonbeliever who accepts them handles life better than a Muslim who does not.

outline.heading: Mediocrity: vanity blocks your potential
outline.gist: Reaching one's potential requires full effort, which most people never risk.

outline.heading: Full effort makes you vulnerable
outline.gist: Giving your all lets others judge your best; accepting that most of us are average is itself freedom from an inflated ego.

outline.heading: The vain either crown their work or hold back
outline.gist: They declare their effort the best and dismiss critics, or invest only a safe part so failure can be excused.

outline.heading: Invest your heart, welcome critique
outline.gist: Confidence in potential, not in the work, lets you give everything and use feedback to improve over repeated attempts.

outline.heading: Humour as a shield
outline.gist: Boys clown around not from disrespect but to avoid sharing a genuine thought that could be judged.

outline.heading: Solo losses and the lesson of chess
outline.gist: Team losses can be blamed on others; losing a chess tournament, which he played competitively, leaves no excuse and teaches tazkiyah like nothing else.

outline.heading: Feedback improves the work, not the self-image
outline.gist: With the ego detached, criticism stings briefly but builds character; he has seen young people grow by risking it.

outline.heading: Kind but honest feedback
outline.gist: Polite cultures sandwich criticism or avoid it, leaving people fired or friendless without knowing why; tell the young the truth kindly.

outline.heading: Vanity blinds you to your own flaws
outline.gist: Others often see exactly why someone's life is not working while the person cannot, because vanity covers their eyes.

outline.heading: 'I knew it all along'
outline.gist: An old experiment found most people claimed to have predicted an event falsely reported to them, revealing how we cling to our theories.

outline.heading: Bias is ego invested in a thought
outline.gist: Detaching ego from thoughts makes thinking flexible; otherwise we wait for a chance to say we were right.

outline.heading: A Muslim pursues truth, not validation
outline.gist: He changes his worldview to fit Islam rather than mining Islam for his own; some listeners stay only until he contradicts them.

outline.heading: Replace the need for vanity
outline.gist: Vanity stays in the nafs, but its need is replaced by confidence in Allah-given potential and by gratitude that redirects praise to Him.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Vanity is claiming credit for outcomes we cannot measure; praise Allah and ask Him to credit us.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: We are entitled to nothing from Allah in this life; entitlement breeds resentment and shaken faith.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Trials are the one worldly promise; serenity comes from understanding, not from exemption.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Have hopes and dua toward Allah, not expectations; keep expectations of people modest and of yourself high.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Spouses must align expectations; the Quran keeps duties minimal and the rest is generosity.

themes.label: Work ethic, productivity and excellence (itqan)
themes.note: Vanity breeds mediocrity by making people hold back effort; invest heart not ego and seek honest feedback.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Vanity blinds us to flaws and binds us to our own theories; a Muslim pursues truth over validation.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Gratitude and confidence in one's potential replace the need for vanity.

People will not be left to say 'we believe' without being tested

hadith.gist: Three things destroy: avarice that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and a man's admiration of himself

maxims: Good assumptions about others, low estimates about yourself

stories.point: Our complaints to Allah over one missing thing look far worse.
Demanding more from Allah after a setback ignores the unpayable debt of life.

stories.who: Psychology experiment on 'I knew it all along'

contemporary: Canadian reluctance to give critical feedback and the feedback sandwich

takeaways: Praise Allah for your successes and ask Him to credit you rather than claiming credit
Stop treating good deeds as a contract that entitles you to worldly outcomes
Replace expectations of Allah with hope and dua; lower expectations of people

Be willing to abandon your own views when the truth points elsewhere

12:33.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجۡنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَيۡهِۖ وَإِلَّا تَصۡرِفۡ عَنِّي كَيۡدَهُنَّ أَصۡبُ إِلَيۡهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
12:33.en: He said: O my Lord! Prison is more dear than that unto which they urge me, and if Thou fend not off their wiles from me I shall incline unto them and become of the foolish

12:34.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنۡهُ كَيۡدَهُنَّۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
12:34.en: So his Lord heard his prayer and fended off their wiles from him. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower

12:35.ar: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَيَسۡجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينࣲ‏
12:35.en: And it seemed good to them (the men-folk) after they had seen the signs (of his innocence) to imprison him for a time

12:36.ar: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجۡنَ فَتَيَانِۖ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَعۡصِرُ خَمۡرࣰ اۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡأٓخَرُ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَحۡمِلُ فَوۡقَ رَأۡسِي خُبۡزࣰ ا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ مِنۡهُۖ نَبِّئۡنَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
12:36.en: And two young men went to prison with him. One of them said: I dreamed that I was pressing wine. The other said: I dreamed that I was carrying upon my head bread whereof the birds were eating. Announce unto us the interpretation, for we see thee of those good (at interpretation)

12:37.ar: قَالَ لَا يَأۡتِيكُمَا طَعَامࣱ تُرۡزَقَانِهِۦٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأۡتُكُمَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّيٓۚ إِنِّي تَرَكۡتُ مِلَّةَ قَوۡمࣲ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
12:37.en: He said: The food which ye are given (daily) shall not come unto you but I shall tell you the interpretation ere it cometh unto you. This is of that which my Lord hath taught me. Lo! I have forsaken the religion of folk who believe not in Allah and are disbelievers in the Hereafter

12:38.ar: وَٱتَّبَعۡتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَۚ مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
12:38.en: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. It never was for us to attribute aught as partner to Allah. This is of the bounty of Allah unto us (the seed of Abraham) and unto mankind; but most men give not thanks

14:27.ar: يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَۚ وَيَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ
14:27.en: Allah confirmeth those who believe by a firm saying in the life of the world and in the Hereafter, and Allah sendeth wrong-doers astray. And Allah doeth what He will

18:79.ar: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتۡ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكࣱ يَأۡخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصۡبࣰ ا
18:79.en: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the river, and I wished to mar it, for there was a king behind them who is taking every ship by force

18:80.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤۡمِنَيۡنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرۡهِقَهُمَا طُغۡيَٰنࣰ ا وَكُفۡرࣰ ا
18:80.en: And as for the lad, his parents were believers and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief

18:81.ar: فَأَرَدۡنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُ زَكَوٰةࣰ وَأَقۡرَبَ رُحۡمࣰ ا
18:81.en: And we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in purity and nearer to mercy

93:3.en: Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee

93:4.en: And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former

93:5.en: And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content

WIBguZvISys.speaker: adnan
WIBguZvISys.speaker_note: his Arabic tafsir halaqah on Surat Yusuf, continuing from 12:35
WIBguZvISys.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Yusuf (12:33-38)
WIBguZvISys.one_line: Prison as Allah's answer to Yusuf's prayer, why morals allow no excuses, the prison companions' dreams, and why ethics need a creed.
WIBguZvISys.summary: He returns to Yusuf's plea and Allah's answer: the answer was nine years of unjust prison. Even a heart full of fear of Allah stays human and weak, as the story of Abdullah ibn Hudhafah shows, and sin never happens in one leap but through small steps that start with inclining. Allah often shows mercy through what looks like punishment, as with Khidr's ship and the boy. The surah's aim is moral constancy: unlike fiqh, where scholars weigh considerations and differ, honesty, chastity and justice admit no bargaining, and when you fall you should admit it plainly instead of justifying it. In the prison scenes he discusses prison in Islamic law as a limited corrective penalty, how broken homes and societies feed modern prisons, and when dreams carry meaning. Yusuf promises to answer the two young men before their next meal but first, with good manners, calls them to Allah, crediting his knowledge to his Lord rather than complaining about his own injustice. Leaving the creed of those who reject Allah and the Hereafter, he grounds ethics in belief: a moral system cannot survive cut off from its creed, and a society that keeps the morals while dropping the belief will lose both.

outline.heading: The proof of his Lord was rooted, not momentary
outline.gist: His understanding of Allah's proofs had built up fear and sincerity that held him back from sin.

outline.heading: No human is free of weakness
outline.gist: Purifying the self frees it from instinct ruling it, but it does not make you a wall.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Hudhafah before the Roman king
outline.gist: Starved, offered wine and pork, then a woman, he refused; he wept only for deeds he had missed, and won the release of all prisoners.

outline.heading: Yusuf knew his own weakness
outline.gist: Allah keeps the believers firm, yet Yusuf asked for protection because he felt himself beginning to weaken.

outline.heading: Sin comes by steps: what 'asbu ilayhinna' means
outline.gist: No one falls in one stroke; soft speech, flirting, online messages and glances open the way over months or years.

outline.heading: Wisdom and knowledge given at maturity
outline.gist: Yusuf's judgment let him see where small steps lead; jahl here is ignorant conduct, not lack of knowledge.

outline.heading: 'His Lord answered him': an uplifting verse answered by prison
outline.gist: After pages of pain the verse lifts the spirit; the next verse shows the answer was imprisonment.

outline.heading: Mercy that looks like punishment
outline.gist: Many people think a trial is bad luck or anger when it is a great mercy.

outline.heading: Khidr's ship and the boy
outline.gist: The parents and the boat owner grieved what was in fact Allah's protection.

outline.heading: The price was disobeying Allah, so he refused
outline.gist: One sin would have given him comfort, power and freedom; he knew right from wrong and would not pay that price.

outline.heading: Morals have no 'considerations' as fiqh does
outline.gist: In fiqh the schools weigh evidence and differ; fornication is simply forbidden at any age or circumstance.

outline.heading: The aim of the surah: moral constancy
outline.gist: Not chastity alone: he never bargains on principle or wrongs others because others wronged him.

outline.heading: Even those entrusted with you may harm you
outline.gist: The brothers were meant to be his guardians; the harm may never stop, yet Islam keeps you upright.

outline.heading: When you slip, do not justify it
outline.gist: Your circumstances are never worse than Yusuf's; admit the wrong with no excuse so repentance and steadiness can follow.

outline.heading: We fight over fiqh and lose the agreed morals
outline.gist: The imams never differed on honesty, trust or justice, yet we split over minor rulings while basic ethics erode.

outline.heading: You do not know what is mercy for you
outline.gist: Allah has not abandoned you; what befalls you may be the answer to a prayer you made.

outline.heading: A new stage: the two young men in prison
outline.gist: Each verse shows Yusuf climbing higher on the ladder of character.

outline.heading: Reading Hafs by Shatibiyyah and the length of madd
outline.gist: The Quran has about a thousand reading paths; here every madd is four counts, and one should learn the long madd before shortening it.

outline.heading: Two youths enter prison with him
outline.gist: Prison cuts a person off from the sun and the world; it is among the worst human experiences.

outline.heading: Prison in Islamic law
outline.gist: Most scholars accept it as a discretionary penalty below the hudud, tied to reform, and reject life-destroying terms.

outline.heading: Society produces its prisoners
outline.gist: Many grew up in broken homes and violent surroundings; Yusuf's steadiness came from prophetic upbringing.

outline.heading: Prisons as places of guidance
outline.gist: Cut off from distraction, many prisoners reflect and accept Islam; prison should reform and return people to society.

outline.heading: When a dream counts
outline.gist: Only a repeated dream is a ru'ya; most concern the past, few the future, and the dream book attributed to Ibn Sirin is not his.

outline.heading: 'We see you are one of the muhsinin'
outline.gist: Between people, ihsan means visible skill and good upbringing, distinct from the ihsan Allah rewards.

outline.heading: Ta'wil means interpretation
outline.gist: News channels live on analysts who interpret events after the fact, with no benefit to the people.

outline.heading: First view: an answer before the next meal
outline.gist: He needed time to ask about each man's situation before interpreting.

outline.heading: Second view: teaching them induction
outline.gist: He could read even the meals and their timing; induction from evidence also appears in the shirt test.

outline.heading: Courtesy before answering
outline.gist: He reassures them he will answer, then asks leave to share something first; callers often skip what the listener came for.

outline.heading: His first act in prison was dawah, not complaint
outline.gist: Unlike those who have objected to Allah in recent years over unanswered prayers, he did not protest.

outline.heading: He did not know how his story would end
outline.gist: We read it knowing the happy ending; he knew only that he was jailed, shamed and far from his parents.

outline.heading: A clear principle carries into every new situation
outline.gist: He could have told his own story or dismissed them; he took the chance to bring two youths to Allah.

outline.heading: 'That is from what my Lord taught me'
outline.gist: He credits his knowledge to Allah, not to his own intelligence.

outline.heading: Leaving the creeds of Egypt
outline.gist: The rulers lacked belief in the resurrection and the Copts held shirk; he followed neither.

outline.heading: The creed of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub
outline.gist: His forefathers' way and the refusal of shirk is Allah's favour on people, though most are not grateful.

outline.heading: Morals cannot exist without a creed
outline.gist: Your understanding of existence produces your ethics; societies that keep the morals but drop the belief lose them in time.

outline.heading: Belief in Allah demands a matching ethic
outline.gist: You cannot affirm Allah and the Last Day and make the forbidden a way of life; mistakes differ from a lifestyle.

outline.heading: A split society
outline.gist: Prayer beads and beards beside lying, backbiting and envy; and atheists who preach ethics from a meaningless universe.

outline.heading: Borrowed ethics without their foundation
outline.gist: Even atheist philosophers admit the problem; a secular country running on Judeo-Christian ethics; Yusuf grounds his morals in creed.

outline.heading: Outro

13:19.ar: ۞أَفَمَن يَعۡلَمُ أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ كَمَنۡ هُوَ أَعۡمَىٰٓۚ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
13:19.en: Is he who knoweth that what is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the truth like him who is blind? But only men of understanding heed

13:20.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَنقُضُونَ ٱلۡمِيثَٰقَ
13:20.en: Such as keep the pact of Allah, and break not the covenant

13:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ وَيَخَافُونَ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
13:21.en: Such as unite that which Allah hath commandeth should be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread a woeful reckoning

13:22.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ سِرࣰّ ا وَعَلَانِيَةࣰ وَيَدۡرَءُونَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
13:22.en: Such as persevere in seeking their Lord's Countenance and are regular in prayer and spend of that which We bestow upon them secretly and openly, and overcome evil with good. Theirs will be the sequel of the (heavenly) Home

13:23.ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدۡنࣲ يَدۡخُلُونَهَا وَمَن صَلَحَ مِنۡ ءَابَآئِهِمۡ وَأَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَذُرِّيَّٰتِهِمۡۖ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَدۡخُلُونَ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن كُلِّ بَابࣲ‏
13:23.en: Gardens of Eden which they enter, along with all who do right of their fathers and their helpmeets and their seed. The angels enter unto them from every gate

13:24.ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُم بِمَا صَبَرۡتُمۡۚ فَنِعۡمَ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
13:24.en: (Saying): Peace be unto you because ye persevered. Ah, passing sweet will be the sequel of the (heavenly) Home

8:2.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ زَادَتۡهُمۡ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
8:2.en: They only are the (true) believers whose hearts feel fear when Allah is mentioned, and when His revelations are recited unto them they increase their faith, and who trust in their Lord

8:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
8:3.en: Who establish worship and spend of that We have bestowed on them

13:25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّعۡنَةُ وَلَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ ٱلدَّارِ
13:25.en: And those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah hath commanded should be joined, and make mischief in the earth: theirs is the curse and theirs the ill abode

4:21.ar: وَكَيۡفَ تَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ وَقَدۡ أَفۡضَىٰ بَعۡضُكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَأَخَذۡنَ مِنكُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظࣰ ا
4:21.en: How can ye take it (back) after one of you hath gone in unto the other, and they have taken a strong pledge from you

4:108.ar: يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمۡ إِذۡ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرۡضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطًا
4:108.en: They seek to hide from men and seek not to hide from Allah. He is with them when by night they hold discourse displeasing unto Him. Allah ever surroundeth what they do

w4K7e6p1-EE.title: AI vs SI: Artificial Intelligence and Spiritual Intelligence
w4K7e6p1-EE.one_line: Guest khutbah contrasting artificial intelligence with the spiritual intelligence of the people of understanding in Surat ar-Ra'd 19-25.
w4K7e6p1-EE.summary: A guest khutbah that sets artificial intelligence against spiritual intelligence. The khatib notes predictions that AI will compete with human intelligence within decades and that students who entered university during COVID and leaned on AI are now struggling and unprepared for life. Against this he reads Surat ar-Ra'd 19-24 as the Quran's portrait of real intelligence, the people of understanding: those who know that revelation is the truth rather than being blind to it, who keep their covenants and promises, who join the ties of kinship Allah ordered joined, who fear their Lord and the evil reckoning, who are patient seeking His face, who establish prayer rather than merely perform it, who spend openly and in secret, and who repel evil with good even though answering bad behaviour in kind is far easier. Their reward is the final home, Gardens of Eden entered with righteous parents, spouses and children, greeted by angels for their patience. The second khutbah turns to the next verse, those who break Allah's covenant, sever ties and spread corruption, applied to how easily spouses break the solemn marriage covenant, and closes with the reminder that AI may impress people but Allah witnesses what people hide from everyone else.

outline.heading: Opening
Will artificial intelligence rival ours?
outline.gist: The khatib raises artificial intelligence and the prediction that by around 2047 AI will compete with human intelligence.

outline.heading: The people of understanding
outline.gist: Against machine intelligence he sets the Quranic phrase ulu al-albab, the people of understanding, and turns to Surat ar-Ra'd, the Thunder, for their portrait.

outline.heading: Ar-Ra'd 13:19-24: the traits and their reward
outline.gist: He recites the passage: is the one who knows the revelation is the truth like the blind; those who fulfil Allah's covenant, join what He ordered joined, fear their Lord, are patient seeking His face, establish prayer, spend secretly and openly and repel evil with good, and their reward of the Gardens of Eden.

outline.heading: Students hollowed out by AI
outline.gist: Educators report that students who entered university during COVID and discovered they could do their work through AI are struggling badly and are not getting an education that prepares them to face life; what is needed is spiritual intelligence.

outline.heading: Seeing the truth and keeping covenants
outline.gist: Spiritual intelligence begins with knowing that what was sent down from your Lord is the absolute truth, unlike those blind to it, and shows in keeping promises, vows, covenants and agreements.

outline.heading: Joining what Allah ordered joined
outline.gist: The people of understanding maintain the ties Allah commanded to be joined: blood relationships and every relationship we are obliged to keep.

outline.heading: Fear of the Lord and the evil reckoning
outline.gist: They fear their Lord and dread the evil reckoning; he pairs it with Al-Anfal 8:2-3, the believers whose hearts tremble at Allah's mention, whose faith grows when His verses are recited, and who rely on Him, pray and spend.

outline.heading: Patience seeking His face
outline.gist: Those who are patient seeking the face of their Lord, which he connects to Gaza and to this generation.

outline.heading: Establishing prayer, not performing it
outline.gist: The verse says they establish the prayer, not merely perform it, and spend from what Allah provides, secretly and openly.

outline.heading: Repelling evil with good
outline.gist: It is easy to answer someone who offends or pushes you with the same behaviour and hard to answer with good, which is what the people of understanding do.

outline.heading: The final home
outline.gist: Theirs is the final home: Gardens of Eden entered with the righteous among their parents, spouses and children, with angels entering from every gate saying peace be upon you for your patience.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those who break the covenant: marriage
outline.gist: Ar-Ra'd 13:25: those who break Allah's covenant after ratifying it. He says he personally witnesses how easily husbands and wives break their bond, although Allah called it a solemn covenant.

outline.heading: Severing ties and corrupting the earth
outline.gist: He continues through the verse: those who sever what Allah ordered joined, cutting one another off, and spread corruption in the land.

outline.heading: AI may impress others, but Allah witnesses
outline.gist: For them is the curse and the evil home. AI may impress others, but everything is witnessed by Allah: An-Nisa 4:108, they hide from people but cannot hide from Allah, who is with them as they plot what He dislikes.

outline.heading: Outro
